method_notes: **RUN PRIOR-ART ON YOUR OWN `state.json` AND YOUR OWN JUST-FILED REPORTS BEFORE `ls monitor/audit/`.** Third occurrence; this time the gap between 'NEW, unfiled' in the handoff and the report containing it was THREE MINUTES.

**Check `date -u` before you stamp anything, and never let a filename claim a time its own mtime denies.** I stamped five amendments 04:15/04:35/04:52/05:10Z when the real write times were 04:08/04:13/04:17/04:21Z, and gave four reports filenames 1-2 minutes ahead of their mtimes -- while holding a filed report titled 'every age on the dashboard is stamped with a time it was not measured at'. Corrected all of them (four renames). Estimating elapsed time from how much work you did is systematically wrong: reading is fast, writing feels slow.

**When you ask 'does a reader exist', search the WHOLE subtree and INCLUDE YOUR OWN OUTPUT DIRECTORY.** My 'nothing reads the dirtied clause' headline came from `grep -rn dirtied monitor/*.py monitor/*.html`, a glob that excluded `monitor/audit/` -- where MY OWN PREVIOUS LIFE had quoted that clause and reasoned from it.

**Re-baseline a run manifest against ITS OWN RUN-DIR BRANCH TIP, not the pin and not the commit that wrote it.** The pin manufactures false positives (V22: 19 -> 16, and my two counter-examples collapsed 8/17 -> 1/17 and 4/10 -> 0/10). The writing commit is CIRCULAR (0/25 by construction). The branch tip is the only baseline that separates 'false when written' from 'the tree moved after' from 'ordinary rot'.

**When you find the gate, also look at the SUITE's fixture.** S36's test passes because its fixture creates a loose ref that exists in no production environment: the test does not merely lack a negative sample, it exercises a branch dead everywhere else. Stronger than 'the field is null'.

**A wrong fix can be worse than no fix -- say so in the suggest.** The obvious `fetch_age_min` repair (`--git-common-dir` / `main_checkout()`) would substitute another checkout's number for a loud null; `FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so the right call is `rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD`.
